body: What was the bug? Anything I can help fix? I can't see the linked ticket.
author: devongovett

body: It wasn't a bug, it's just that lightningcss is more restrictive than swc_css, so technically invalid syntax that swc_css was handling gracefully was failing hard with lightningcss. What we'll probably end up doing for now is enabling lightningcss behind a flag instead of doing a direct swap. Ideally, we'll be able to make lightningcss the default and remove swc_css when we release the next major version.
author: padmaia

body: What was the syntax error in particular? Not sure if you tried already, but there's also an [error recovery](https://lightningcss.dev/docs.html#error-recovery) option which is more lenient in parsing. Maybe that could also help.
author: devongovett

body: Oh interesting... I'm not sure if the team tried that already either, I'll dig and get back to you.

mkdir foo

node index.js

@ijjk I can't edit labels myself. This PR is not about documentation (though I added some documentation to reflect the code change). It is about changing Next.js `route.ts` type definition to allow custom exports. Which is not currently possible.

Also the discussion (https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/55140) hasn't been picked up by anybody, do you know if I could mention someone who could be interested in having a look at my proposal ?

body:
@theo-lubert 

> Some cases require to export some info: data, configs, types for the client, etc...

Wouldn't you want these `/lib` type of logic in a separate directory? 

> could enable a lot of nice features (especially around type inference imo).

Is it possible to elaborate on this (versus having like a separate `types.ts` file)?

> Next.js currently forces us to create separate files

Is the issue because the thought is you _can't_ export multiple methods in a Route Handler?
author: samcx
theo-lubert

body: Hi @samcx @leerob  what can we do to make this happen ? or at least move in any direction ? A year is a long time. It really is a small change. Thx a lot
author: theo-lubert

body: We don't have precedent for this type of change. As this problem is solvable by placing the other exports within a separate file (the `/lib` solution), I'd suggest that we don't proceed with this change.
author: wyattjoh

body:
Moving to `/lib` doesn't solve this imo, as the relevant data still is in `route.ts` (we want to infer types and data from it)

Best case scenario, you can move the code in another file colocated in the same dir.
This means `route.ts` basically becomes a one liner that export the methods form another file. This duplication doesn't feel right to me. And making `route.ts` more extensible is a good way to solve this.

`_` prefix seems resonable, as its usually meaning is "ignore this"

Do you see any risk in allowing us to extend `route.ts` this way ?
author: theo-lubert

body: Adding sever-only helps avoid file misuse. If all i18n dictionaries leak to the browser, bundle size will get huge. The import helps to prevent this.
author: kachkaev

body: It looks like the redirect functions are hardcoded to `307`/`308` redirects. How do you do `301`/`302`/`303` redirects then?
author: GabenGar

body:
> Why does Next.js use 307 and 308? Traditionally a 302 was used for a temporary redirect, and a 301 for a permanent redirect, but many browsers changed the request method of the redirect to GET, regardless of the original method. For example, if the browser made a request to POST /v1/users which returned status code 302 with location /v2/users, the subsequent request might be GET /v2/users instead of the expected POST /v2/users. Next.js uses the 307 temporary redirect, and 308 permanent redirect status codes to explicitly preserve the request method used.

From the docs 🙏
author: leerob

body: Yeah but there might be use cases for when you want to change the method to `GET` and `301`/`302`/`303` are go-to SEO redirects (SEO doesn't operate outside of `GET` requests anyway). I have a suspicion some search engines can choke on `307`/`308` by assuming these are invalid codes.

> FYI I have removed `__NEXT_PRIVATE_PREBUNDLED_REACT` in #55762

`__NEXT_PRIVATE_PREBUNDLED_REACT` is the env I have encountered with `worker_threads`, yet many more env used internally by Next.js need to be passed down to build/route workers (`__NEXT_PRIVATE_CROSSORIGIN`, `__NEXT_ANALYTICS_ID`, etc.).

`pnpm test-start test/production/ci-missing-typescript-deps/index.test.ts` one failed because there's throwing a new error introduced before 27.0.0. 

https://github.com/jestjs/jest/blob/6c83c0f91d219771d6c0c2ce32231053cae322b5/packages/jest-worker/src/workers/ChildProcessWorker.ts#L185-L189
author: huozhi

body:
> `pnpm test-start test/production/ci-missing-typescript-deps/index.test.ts` one failed because there's throwing a new error introduced before 27.0.0.
> 
> https://github.com/jestjs/jest/blob/6c83c0f91d219771d6c0c2ce32231053cae322b5/packages/jest-worker/src/workers/ChildProcessWorker.ts#L185-L189

The real cause of the CI failure is the inproper handling of the worker exiting.

I've fixed that in [`7bd1a95` (#55257)](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/55257/commits/7bd1a95cc326a7d1ebe9fd9eb681d577e7bdef1d).

body: I assume this restriction can be removed once Progressive Enhancement functionality has been implemented?
author: brhx

body:
> I assume this restriction can be removed once Progressive Enhancement functionality has been implemented?

Progressive enhancement isn't inherently connected with server/client components. It's a hook so it won't be possible to run it inside of server components. It holds state basically. Progressive enhancement means that it will work with non-hydrated submissions and the state will be correctly forwarded to next render.
author: pawelblaszczyk5
brhx

body:
> @pawelblaszczyk5 Hooks are not inherently restricted to only client components / SSR. In any case, the `useFormState` hook will have different implementations depending on call context:
> 
> > When used in combination with Server Actions, it will also support progressive enhancement — a form that is submitted before it has hydrated will have its state transferred to the next page. However, like the other action-related hooks, it works with fully client-driven actions, too.
> 
> [facebook/react#27270](https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/27270)

Afaik (what I understand from all the PRs in React repo), this hook is client only by design. And the progressive enhancement story refers to passing server action as the parameter. Then, it'll be possible to pass previous submission state to methods responsible for rendering on server and hydrating on client (this part will be handled by Next.js under the hood). This is referred as a `postback` state and will get matched to the same hook instance within next MPA render by emitting special markers. This allows you carrying state between MPA renders in progressively enhnaced manner.

body:
Ah it appears I've maybe conflated the two. From the Next.js docs:

> Displaying loading or error states currently requires using Client Components. We are exploring options for server-side functions to retrieve these values as we move forward in stability for Server Actions.

I was assuming that `useFormState` _was_ this server-side function (as well as a client-side one), but this isn't gonna be the function that allows for data to be returned from [server-only forms](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/data-fetching/forms-and-mutations#server-only-forms)? If I understand correctly, this still requires a client component, it will just now also work with PE.

body: The default for `.next/standalone/server.js` is now `0.0.0.0`, so you may as well delete `ENV HOSTNAME` altogether.
author: DuCanhGH

body:
> The default for `.next/standalone/server.js` is now `0.0.0.0`, so you may as well delete `ENV HOSTNAME` altogether.

You are right in that the default hostname value for the standalone server is 0.0.0.0, however the current value used in the dockerfile is incorrect, so for one using this example the server will fail to be accessible from the outside of the container.
author: DragosMocrii

body:
@DragosMocrii well I mentioned deleting that value, right? Sometimes the deployment platform just provides `HOSTNAME` for you (otherwise the default value `0.0.0.0` should just work), and you'd only need to have `ENV HOSTNAME 0.0.0.0` if that value isn't actually meant to be a hostname. Though, maybe adding a comment like this would be nice:
```
# Uncomment the following line if `process.env.HOSTNAME` is not provided by your provider
# or it is an invalid value for a hostname.
# ENV HOSTNAME 0.0.0.0
```
This is just my suggestion though, feel free to do it how you want :) It'd be nice if you could change this for other Docker examples as well (they should be close to this example).
author: DuCanhGH

body:
@DuCanhGH sorry, I missed your initial point. I've made the updates per your suggestion.

author: leerob

body:
@leerob Thanks, I will play around with `useFormState` and check if I can build my use case with it. The interesting question for me is: ***"Is it possible to change/reset the `state` that is provided by `useFromState` from a source that is not that useFormState's `formAction`?"*** 

Scenario:
1) I want to open a Toast notification when the `state` of `useFormState` becomes a certain value by executing the `formAction`. (This part is covered by the docs and should work fine.)
 2) When the user clicks on a Cancel-Icon inside that Toast Notification I want to reset the state **without executing the `formAction`** or any other Server-side code. (This part is not covered yet.)
author: ghost

body:
While I really see the benefit of the `useFormState` API, I am glad that I had already seen the example that @schimi-dev already mentioned. It was really an eye-opener to me that the server actions can be used as 'simple functions' and that this is not something that always needs to be triggered by a form action.

I am currently working on migrating some pages to the app-structure, and I was missing this example today. Glad I found this PR so I know I didn't make this functionality up ;-)

I also think it would be great to provide a (simple) example that doesn't work with a `<form>` tag. For example, I am implementing a QR code scanner, which doesn't use a `<form>` underneath. Using server actions is great, but according to the new docs I would not know that that's possible.

PD:

I don't know how it happened and the variable window.__BUILD_MANIFEST.__rewrites is an array instead of afterFiles, beforeFiles, fallback object.

But the error I experienced can be easily reproduced by entering this code in the console in a Next application:

__BUILD_MANIFEST.__rewrites = __BUILD_MANIFEST.__rewrites.afterFiles
author: mdjfs

body:
I confirm, that bug is for cache problems.

When this error happens, usually DevTools/Sources/[page]/[page]-app/_next/static/[appbuild]-/_buildManifest.js has an array in __rewrites instead of an object.

I just don't know when the bundler decides to rebuild everything or not. Surely not, and in production it is very difficult to detect these problems and know that the entire application must be rebuilt.

body:
Yes of course. Is complicated to reproduce because the main reason of the bug is the browsers cache for the _buildManifest.js. 

The steps for reproduce are:

1. Start a project with a two pages and `<Link>` component in each one 
2. Write a next.config.js with a rewrites array 
3. Install next^9, react^16 and rest of dependencies
4. Build and start the project and go to localhost:3000
5. Try links 
6. Upgrade next to latest version, also with react
7. Build and start the projcet and go to localhost:3000
8. Try again links, not working because browser fetchs the old version of _buildManifest.js and fails

I'll include scripts to reproduce this steps. How to use:

1. Open 'test-next-reproduce'
2. Run 'node install-and-test.js'
3. Try links
4. Run 'node upgrade-and-test.js'
5. Try links again, not working

author: Inzendis

body:
This was reverted in https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/55764. `reader.closed` is a Promise, not a boolean, so `!reader.closed` is always falsey. The end result is that we would never canceled the stream.

The bug is not actually in Next.js, it's in React's server streaming. We've pinged them, and they're looking into t.

body:
> How did you figure out that it was on React's side?

The stack traces included on https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/55608 point to React's code. It can't have been on our side, cancelling a response stream is a normal operation that needs to be handled. So the source must of been whatever is pushing the data from: 

```
    at ReadableByteStreamController.enqueue (node:internal/webstreams/readablestream:1150:13)
    at /path/to/app/readable-error/node_modules/next/dist/compiled/next-server/app-page.runtime.dev.js:1:447268
```

but this is very very simple:

I've commented to https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/54961, this PR is causing the environment variable `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` to always be overridden even when you are not using the `--experimental-https` flag.

I suppose the env-var should only be set if you also passed something to fill it with, or at least check if there is something in it already?

It is happening on this line: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/55775/files#diff-ddadbe5e107283e1bda7713050b8dcc19065dc804ab082e55e148efac0ef0221R255

**Orb Code Review** (powered by GLM 5.1 on [Orb Cloud](https://orbcloud.dev))

Reviewed the fix to prevent infinite redirects to i18n subdomains.

### The fix

Changes `self.location.hostname` → `self.location.host` in the i18n domain redirect guard.

### Why this fixes the bug

`location.hostname` strips the port, so if `detectedDomain.domain` is configured as `localhost:3000`, the comparison `location.hostname` (`localhost`) !== `detectedDomain.domain` (`localhost:3000`) would always be `true`, triggering a hard navigation redirect on every page load → infinite redirects.

Using `location.host` (which includes non-default ports) fixes this by making the comparison include the port.

### ⚠️ Minor edge case to consider

If a user configures `domain: 'example.com'` (without port) but accesses the site at `http://example.com:3000`, the new comparison would be `example.com:3000 !== example.com` → `true`, potentially triggering a redirect that wouldn't have occurred before. This is an edge case that primarily affects development setups, and the fix correctly prioritizes resolving the infinite redirect bug.

---

**Summary:** Correct one-line fix that resolves infinite redirect loops in i18n subdomain routing by including the port in domain comparison. The trade-off is reasonable.

**Assessment: approve**

**Orb Code Review** (powered by GLM 5.1 on [Orb Cloud](https://orbcloud.dev))

Reviewed the modularize imports configuration update for `ahooks`.

### What changed

1. Switches import paths from `ahooks/es/` to `ahooks/lib/`
2. Adds explicit mappings for `configResponsive` and `useResponsive` (both from `ahooks/lib/useResponsive`)
3. Updates wildcard `*` mapping to use `ahooks/lib/{{member}}`

### 💡 Observation

The `/es/` → `/lib/` path change is the most significant part. This suggests `ahooks` may have changed their package structure or the ES module directory doesn't contain all expected subpath exports. This is a reasonable fix.

**Question for the author:** Have you verified this works with the latest `ahooks` version? It would be helpful to confirm which version(s) of `ahooks` this config targets, since the `es/` → `lib/` change could affect tree-shaking behavior for users on older versions.

### ✅ Pattern looks correct

The shared module mapping for `configResponsive`/`useResponsive` is a valid pattern. The `createUpdateEffect` mapping correctly preserves `from=named&as=default`, while the new entries without it should work if those are default exports.

---

**Summary:** Configuration update that adjusts ahooks modularize imports from `/es/` to `/lib/` paths and adds missing mappings. Looks reasonable but would benefit from version compatibility confirmation.

**Assessment: approve**
